documents.unit: Office of the Vice Provost for Academic Affairs
documents.title: AI Use Guidelines
documents.summary: The Vice Provost hub page frames Ball State's AI guidelines as living and sets one student expectation: follow the instructor's selected GenAI statement and the Student Academic Ethics Policy. The detailed instructor, research, administrative and misuse guidelines are only linked and were not accessible.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no university-wide stance; it says completion of student checkers "does not automatically mean GenAI use is permitted" and that students "must still follow the GenAI Statement their instructor selected", handing the decision to instructors.

units.why: The page frames the guidelines as helping the community use GenAI "responsibly and ethically", an institution-level statement of purpose and scope, so P56 (framework/preamble) with actor all and general phase; it sets no rule itself.
units.anchor: to help our community use Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools responsibly and ethically
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on every code (P56, informs, all, general); only topics differed. Final topics kept to the starter codebook.

units.why: 'living guidelines ... continuously updated ... subject to change' says the policy is provisional and will be revised, which is P54; the email address invites feedback.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P54, informs, admin, over-time; no disagreement. Wording of anchor taken from the source.
units.anchor: These are living guidelines and are continuously updated as new information is received.
units.frag_end: All information is subject to change.

units.why: "For feedback and questions, please email ai@bsu.edu" invites feedback on the guidelines, which P54 lists ("feedback is invited"); addressed to the whole community.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A made this unit; coder B folded the email into the 'living guidelines' unit. The source says 'For feedback and questions, please email: ai@bsu.edu', an invitation to give feedback, which P54 covers ('feedback is invited'). Kept as a real, separate statement.
units.anchor: For feedback and questions, please email
units.frag_start: For feedback and questions, please email

units.why: 'students are encouraged to complete Step 1 ... Step 2' asks students to run self-check tools before using GenAI for coursework. P10 is about asking the instructor, which is different, and no other type covers a pre-use self-check, so UNCOVERED.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on UNCOVERED, should, student, during-work. They differed on unit_stance (A permit, B neutral). The sentence recommends a self-check only 'if generative AI use is permitted' and itself neither allows nor bans AI, so neutral. B's normalized wording follows the source and is kept.

units.policy: If generative AI use is permitted, students are encouraged to complete Step 1 (Should I use AI?) and Step 2 (How should I use AI responsibly?) before using GenAI tools for coursework.
units.uncovered_note: Students are encouraged to complete two self-check tools (Should I use AI? / How should I use AI responsibly?) before using GenAI for coursework.

units.why: 'does not automatically mean GenAI use is permitted on every assignment' leaves permission to be decided assignment by assignment. P04 fits (per-assignment decision); P11 does not because it is about checkers, not carry-over between courses.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P04, informs, student. Phase differed (A during-work, B course-start). The sentence tells students that finishing the self-checks does not settle whether a given assignment allows GenAI, so it applies when a student is deciding about work in progress; the course-start communication is the next sentence (the GenAI Statement). Final: during-work.
units.anchor: Completion of the checkers does not automatically mean GenAI use is permitted on every assignment.

units.why: 'Students must still follow the GenAI Statement their instructor selected for the course' binds students to whatever statement the instructor picked; the university sets no rule itself. That is P04 (instructor sets the rule), with the syllabus statement as the vehicle.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P04, must, student, course-start; only topics differed. Kept B's topics.
units.anchor: Students must still follow the GenAI Statement their instructor selected for the course

units.why: 'assignment-specific directions' must be followed as well, so permissions can differ assignment by assignment and are not set once per course. P04 (per-assignment rule) is chosen over P11 since nothing is said about carry-over.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B made this unit; coder A treated the whole list as one sentence. The sentence lists several things students must follow. 'assignment-specific directions' and 'instructors' guidance' are a separate duty from the GenAI Statement (set once at course start) and from the Ethics Policy, so it is kept as its own P04 unit, during-work.
units.anchor: assignment-specific directions, instructors' guidance
units.policy: Students must still follow assignment-specific directions and instructors' guidance.

units.why: Students must also follow the Student Academic Ethics Policy, which brings AI conduct under the integrity process. P36 is the closest type but the sentence only points to the policy and adds no sanction rule.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P36, must, student, general. Coder A left policy null, but the anchor alone ('Student Academic Ethics Policy') does not state the rule, so B's normalized form is used, without B's added 'when using GenAI for coursework', which the sentence implies but does not state in these words.
units.anchor: Student Academic Ethics Policy
units.policy: Students must still follow Ball State University's Student Academic Ethics Policy.

documents.title: AI Guidelines (AI Initiatives)
documents.summary: Information Technology's AI Guidelines page states seven institutional AI principles, then rules on approved tools, meeting transcription, data classification, retention, sustainability and citation. For coursework it repeats the provost hub and hands the decision to the instructor's GenAI statement.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no course-level stance for student work: it repeats that completion of checkers "does not automatically mean GenAI use is permitted" and that students "must still follow the GenAI Statement their instructor selected". Its own rules concern tools, data and citation, so it delegates.

units.why: The opening says AI has "a profound impact on education, research" and brings challenges that "must be appropriately addressed", an institution-level framing of purpose, so P56.
units.anchor: AI technologies have a profound impact on education, research

units.why: Principle "Excellence" commits to using AI "in ways that align with and uphold our Academic Integrity Policy", a stated institutional principle (P56); the commitment is a principle, not a rule on a specific use.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P56. Modality differed (A should, B informs). 'We commit to using AI in ways that align with and uphold our Academic Integrity Policy' is a statement of institutional value, not an instruction to a named group, so informs. Same rule applied to all the value statements below.
units.anchor: We commit to using AI in ways that align with and uphold our

units.why: Innovation value: 'We commit to responsible AI experimentation and implementation to enhance creativity, learning, and research' welcomes AI use. P02 covers a default that 'allows, welcomes, encourages' AI, and this statement does that, so P02 rather than the generic framework type P56.
units.resolution_why: Type differed (A P56, B P02). P56 is for purpose, scope and principles; P02 is for a rule that welcomes or encourages AI. The sentence's content is welcoming 'responsible AI experimentation and implementation to enhance ... learning', so P02 with encourage stance. Modality informs (agreed).
units.anchor: We commit to responsible AI experimentation and implementation to enhance creativity, learning, and research.

units.why: Courage value: 'We commit to willingly exploring the possibilities within AI while also addressing potential ethical challenges and risks' names ethical challenges and risks of AI as something to address, which is P53; modality informs because it states a value.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on type (A P56, B P53). 'addressing potential ethical challenges and risks' names ethical risk; the principle is about facing risk, which P53 covers, so P53.
units.anchor: willingly exploring the possibilities within AI while also addressing potential ethical challenges and risks

units.why: Principle "Integrity" commits to "upholding human creativity and critical thinking with our AI usage, avoiding misuse"; this expects humans to remain the thinkers, closest to P32 (students stay primary problem-solver) though stated institution-wide.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P32 and informs after reconciliation (A said should, B informs). Value statement, so informs.

units.why: Principle "Inclusiveness" commits to "developing and using AI in accessible and equitable ways", an equity and access commitment (P51).
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P51. Modality differed (A should, B informs); a value commitment, so informs.

units.why: Principle "Gratitude" commits to "valuing collaboration and appreciating the ethical guidelines that shape responsible AI use", another institution-level principle (P56).
units.resolution_why: Only coder A made this unit. The Gratitude value ('valuing collaboration and appreciating the ethical guidelines that shape responsible AI use') is one of the seven stated values, a real framework statement (P56). Kept; informs like the other values.

documents.unit: Office of the Vice Provost, Student Services
documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy
documents.summary: The Academic Integrity page is mostly a general misconduct process. Its AI content tells faculty to state generative-AI expectations on syllabi, points to the Student and Faculty AI guidelines, and recommends two AI-use scales to communicate levels of acceptable use.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no AI stance. It asks faculty to "make explicit on your syllabi ... using generative AI (for the entire course or for specific assignments)", so the rule is left to instructors and courses.

units.why: Step 1 has the instructor request a 'preliminary inquiry meeting', citing the AI misuse guidelines. Talking with the student before any formal allegation is P57. The process is generic to integrity cases and covers AI misuse.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P57, must, instructor, when-misuse. The process is generic to all integrity cases, but Step 1 cites the 'Guidelines for Instructors to Address Suspected AI Misuse', so it is kept as an AI-misuse rule.
units.anchor: instructor and student meet to discuss incident before instructor determines whether a formal allegation

units.why: Faculty are advised to 'make explicit on your syllabi ... your expectations regarding ... using generative AI (for the entire course or for specific assignments)'. This is an AI statement in the syllabus (P09); the course-vs-assignment scope is secondary.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P09, should, instructor. Phase differed (A before-course, B course-start). The rule is about telling students expectations on the syllabus, which is communicating expectations: course-start. Coder A's second unit (P04, 'for the entire course or for specific assignments') is the scope inside this same sentence, not a distinct rule, so it is dropped and the scope is carried in this policy text.
units.anchor: Make explicit on your syllabi and discuss with students your expectations
units.policy: Instructors should make explicit on their syllabi, and discuss with students, their expectations about acceptable and unacceptable actions, especially regarding using generative AI for the entire course or for specific assignments.

units.why: Students are told to "Know when AI tools are permissible and how to properly cite them", which asks students to learn the permission rules and to cite AI use (P24).
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P24, should, student. Phase differed (A general, B during-work). The tip sits under 'Avoid Accidental Plagiarism' and asks students to learn permissibility and cite AI in their work, so during-work. unit_stance differed (A neutral, B permit); the sentence permits nothing itself, so neutral.
units.anchor: Know when AI tools are permissible and how to properly cite them.
units.frag_start: Know when AI tools are permissible

units.why: The page recommends the "Student Generative AI Use Scale" and "AI Assessment Scale" for "communicating to students the varying levels of acceptable AI use", i.e. named levels of AI use, so P05.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P05, instructor, course-start. Modality differed (A may, B informs). The page offers these as 'especially helpful' resources and gives no instruction, so informs.
units.anchor: communicating to students the varying levels of acceptable AI use
units.frag_start: The Student Generative AI Use Scale

notes: Reconciled from coder A and coder B. The detailed instructor, research, administrative and misuse guidelines sit behind an inaccessible SharePoint link, so only the hub text was coded. The provost hub text is repeated on the IT page and coded on each page. Generic integrity-process rules (penalty range, hearing, right to respond, authentic assignments, administrative responsibility) were coded by B only and dropped because the sentences do not mention AI. No school or computing-unit policy was found; course layer is deferred. Topics use the starter codebook in tools/AGENT_BRIEF.md.
